source.title: Knowledge-Aware Neuron Interpretation for Scene Classification
source.authors: Yong Guan; Freddy Lecue; Jiaoyan Chen; Ru Li; Jeff Z. Pan

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a neuron-interpretation tool change improves neuron interpretability, using concept-clustering and IoU rather than the original audit's measure.
record.gate_note: Table 5 reports IoU gains from clustering concepts for ResNet-18 neurons. Other prediction-explanation, model-manipulation, and retraining results are not included because they do not directly measure the versions' claims about neuron interpretability.
record.test_reason: The study builds a knowledge-graph neuron-interpretation framework for ResNet scene classifiers and reports only its own method's gains. Table 5 compares its Concept Filtering against NetDissect labels without clustering, as a relative IoU gain. It never reports the share of interpretable neurons, so the gain cannot show whether the interpretable share rises with better tools (V4). Merging concept labels into fewer clusters can raise IoU by coarsening the label set, not by explaining more neurons. No language models, InceptionV1, attribution graphs or simulation scoring appear.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but too narrow. The authors conclude three things. Knowledge-graph core concepts (SCC/ICC) give better prediction explanations than baselines. Concept Filtering gives over 23% point gain in neuron-concept IoU, best 26.3% with TransE at 168 clusters. Core concepts help manipulate and improve the model, by neuron disabling, re-training, and a PE-feature SVM reaching 26.7% accuracy improvement.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates ConceptNet-based concept clustering and its effect on neuron-concept IoU; it does not perform the original language-model neuron-pole audit or measure shares of interpretable neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: IoU gain varies with embedding method and cluster count; the authors describe optimal performance in the 168–180 cluster range.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet-18 on ADE20k, merging semantically equivalent concept labels via ConceptNet embeddings raises neuron-concept IoU by 17–26% relative to unmerged labels. The authors say this 'exposes more interpretable units' but report no count of units.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coarsening or fusing the concept vocabulary used in network dissection raises neuron-concept alignment scores.

record.problems: The relevant results are from ResNet-18 on ADE20k and report IoU gains, not the proportion of interpretable neurons. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Prediction-explanation metrics, model-manipulation curves, retraining results, and cross-model prediction-explanation results were omitted because they do not directly measure neuron-interpretability shares or the IoU effect in Table 5.

untested.parts: All: no language models, dense or mixture-of-experts.
All: no InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose or superposition analysis.
Share of interpretable neurons under better tools or architectures; causes (architecture, regularization); InceptionV1-sized estimates.
All: no attribution graphs from neurons.
All: no test of explanations predicting held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. The rows are the study's own method against its no-clustering baseline, and the IoU gain is relative, with absolute IoU not stated. No interpretable-neuron share is reported, and label fusion may inflate IoU without making neurons more interpretable. Reclassified as T4 / uses_without_test.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and its reported shares.
Language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, and scaling to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car examples, pose, recursive generalization, and superposition.

The share of neurons that are interpretable; InceptionV1-sized models and the stated 5% to about 99% estimates; architecture and regularization as causes; comparisons across modern architectures or late layers.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and their ability to explain behaviour without a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict new activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-18 on ADE20k, all reported embedding and cluster-count conditions
reader_labels.reason: Every reported clustering condition has a positive IoU gain over no clustering, consistent with improved neuron-interpretation quality; rows r1-r36. This does not establish a higher share of interpretable neurons.
